questions.stem: A 25-year-old woman has visited surgeons’ office because she is worried that she may develop breast cancer as her mother had breast cancer. The surgeon starts eliciting history, which of the following history is irrelevant to rule out a history of familial carcinoma in her?

options.label: A
options.text: Age of onset of carcinoma in mother

options.label: B
options.text: History of carcinoma in any of the family members other than breast

questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) history of metastasis. Familial carcinomas have multiple carcinomas in family, multifocal and bilateral carcinomas also early age of onset. Metastasis can be seen in either sporadic or familial carcinomas.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old male presents with pharyngitis for last 5 days, the patient was started on oral amoxicillin. 3 days later the patient presents with dark coloured urine. Urine examination now shows haemoglobin & no RBC. which of the following is the mechanism of such manifestation?

options.label: D
options.text: Increased excretion of drug in the urine

questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) Type 2 hypersensitivity reaction. So this patient has taken penicillin after which he has presented with hemoglobinuria which suggests there is an intravascular haemolysis. Option C Type 3 hypersensitivity reaction can happen after a post pharyngitis but it will present with hematuria not with hemoglobinuria. Haemoglobinuria suggests intravascular haemolysis. In the above options option B is the only one to cause intravascular haemolysis.

questions.stem: Which phase of wound healing involves the formation of granulation tissue?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Proliferative phase includes proliferation of Epithelium, Blood vessel (granulation tissue) and fibroblast

questions.answerText: Happens in organs where there is rapid pH change

questions.stem: While studying data of a genetic disease a medical student finds that the disease is occurring both in males and females, Females are transmitting disease to sons and daughters, but males are not transmitting disease to their children, however grandchildren of affected males are having disease. Which of the following inheritance is it likely to be

options.label: C
options.text: Maternal deletion in a paternally imprinted gene

options.label: D
options.text: Paternal deletion in a maternally imprinted gene

questions.answerText: Maternal deletion in a paternally imprinted gene
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Disease is being transmitted from females to children and males to grand children which is characteristic of maternally deleted of paternally imprinted gene.

questions.stem: Mechanism of Cancer cells consuming more glucose because

options.label: A
options.text: Lactic acid production in absence of oxugen

options.label: B
options.text: Increased glucose transporters (GLUT) and Oxidative Phosphorylation

options.label: D
options.text: Lactic acid is produced despite presence of oxygen

questions.answerText: Lactic acid is produced despite presence of oxygen
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (D) tumor cells consume more glucose because they have less efficient glucose metabolism glycolysis ( this happens despite adequate oxygen= Aerobic glycolysis)

questions.stem: Assertion (A): ABO matching is not mandatory for hematopoietic stem cell transplant. Reason (R): hematopoietic stem cells do not express ABO antigens.

options.label: A
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are independently true and R is the correct explanation of A

options.label: B
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are independently true and R is not the correct explanation of A

options.label: C
options.text: A is true R is False

options.label: D
options.text: R is true A is false

questions.answerText: Both (A) and (R) are independently true and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (A) ABO is not mandatory in BMT because the stem cells don’t express ABO antigens thus won’t be lysed by anti ABO antibodies

questions.stem: Which enzyme converts arachidonic acid into leukotrienes, contributing to the late-phase of inflammation?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) Lipoxygenase (LOX) is the enzyme responsible for converting arachidonic acid into leukotrienes, which play a role in the late-phase of inflammation and immune response.

questions.stem: Which of the following cell death is associated with cell membrane damage, normal nuclear morphology and inflammation?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (D) Ferroptosis is due to ROS produced from Fe which leads to cell membrane damage, shrunken mitochondria and normal nucleus

questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (A) IL 1 is chemotaxin not chemo kine. Chemokine are cell specific chemotactic agents IL8 (Neutrophils ) Eotaxin (eosinophils) MCP1 , MIP 1 ( monocytes macrophages)

questions.stem: A 16-year-old boy is having episodes of bronchospasm and wheeze after exposure to pollen. The symptoms of wheezing subsided within few hours and after taking salbutamol. Despite taking the drug after 4 days the patient is still having increased cough expectoration and mild dyspnoea. Which of the cell is responsible for current manifestation?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (A) Eosinophil. The patient is having increased expectoration and sputum after 4 or 5 days of an acute episode of bronchospasm this will be a late manifestation of a type I hypersensitivity reaction which are due to eosinophil which secrete eosinophilic cationic protein and major basic proteins which will end up causing tissue destruction, inflammation and increased mucus secretion. On the other hand mast cell occur early, the early phase usually stays for few minutes to few hours after exposure of the antigen which is mediated by histamine which will have bronchospasm and also increased mucus secretion, the late phase typically starts after 1 week and can stay for few days.

questions.stem: In which of the following cellular adaptation is there an increased size of organ due to the increase in number of cells?
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (B) hyperplasia are due to increase in cell number which leads to increased organ size and hypertrophy is increased size of organ due to increased cell size.

questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (A) the left testicular vein drains into renal vein. A renal cell carcinoma can compress into renal vein or even spread into renal vein leading to obstruction which causes varicocele.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old underwent 4/6 HLA matched allogenic renal transplant. A few weeks later he has fever, and he has decreased urine output. A renal biopsy shows inflammation in the renal vessels. Which of the following mechanism is most likely to cause such manifestation

options.label: B
options.text: Anti HLA antibodies from donor killing graft cells

options.text: Anti HLA antibodies from recipient killing graft cells

questions.stem: Ipilimumab is a monoclonal antibody to CTLA-4, what is the likely effect of this drug on cancer cells

options.label: A
options.text: Activates T cells by enhancing MHC-TCR interactions

options.label: C
options.text: Activates T cells by enhancing CD28 -B71 interactions

questions.answerText: Activates T cells by enhancing CD28 -B71 interactions
questions.solutionHtml: Correct Answer (C) CTLA 4 induced by tumor cells binds with B71 and B72 proteins thus not allowing CD28 to interact with B7 proteins (which is needed for T cell activation). Ipilimumab reverses this effect allowing T cell to get activated.
